Senses.Explanation: An accomplished leading master or craftsman of the lineage. Prefaces, patrons, and records use this title to mark recognized mastery and capacity to shape the lineage; it names standing in the house, not an ordinary artisan.

A lineage master: the designation for someone presented or judged in relation to the Chan ancestral line. The term occurs 1,445 times in 257 allowlisted texts. Daowu Wuzhen gives a direct role statement: “As for a lineage master, he takes away the poor child's pearl sewn in his clothes and examines the accomplished person's viewpoint” (夫宗師者，奪貧子之衣珠，究達人之見處). Dahui Zonggao says that a lineage master decides right and wrong and must open people's eyes rather than rely only on blind cangues and sightless blows (大凡宗師決斷是非。要得開人眼目。不可一向盲枷瞎棒). Guishan Lingyou says a lineage master must meet people with the fundamental matter. Yuanwu Keqin likewise says the lineage-master household must teach a person through, even at the cost of injuring hand and blade when the person does not understand (宗師家為人須為教徹). Yuanwu calls Zhaozhou Congshen “a great-handed lineage master” (大手宗師), saying that Zhaozhou does not discuss mystery, marvel, occasion, or object but meets people with the fundamental matter. He also calls Dongshan Shouchu, Zhimen Guangzuo, Deshan Yuanmi, and Xianglin Chengyuan “great lineage masters” (皆為大宗師). The label can be withheld or mocked: Xuedou Chongxian says of an inadequate answer, “calling oneself a lineage master like this and wanting to open the eyes of humans and gods—only in the donkey year” (如此自稱宗師，欲開人天眼目，驢年去). The noun thus works as a title and appraisal tied to public responsibilities, and as a rebuke when a claimant does not meet them.
Senses.Note: All direct-definition formulas and common modifiers were searched. The “great lineage master” form occurs 113 times in 49 texts; the lineage-master-household form occurs 87 times in 47; the lineage-master-eye form occurs 22 times in 20; and the “lineage master of a generation” form occurs nine times in eight. The role is corpus-wide and is not keyed to a single teacher.

Senses.Explanation: The defining purport is the governing point of a lineage or house as transmitted, established, entrusted, and tested in encounters. The exact rows retain their separate speakers, narrators, participants, and quoted layers; no single deployment is made to resolve all others.

The Chan lineage tradition is the inherited school domain invoked when speakers distinguish its characteristic questions, ways, vocabulary, or business from other forms of exposition. The phrase can refer broadly to the tradition or narrowly to what counts within its gate. A book title containing the graphs is not by itself evidence for this common-noun use.
Senses.Note: The frozen corpus has 2,253 exact hits in 312 files representing 306 works. Eight anchors span definitions, questions about lineage business, house comparison, instruction, and direct address across independent works; title-only hits were excluded.

AlternateTargets: the public style of a Chan house
Senses.Explanation: The lineage's house style: the recognizable way a Chan house carries and displays its inheritance. Public interviews repeatedly pair it with the song the named respondent sings and ask from whom it descends. Linji Yixuan answers by recalling his three beatings under Huangbo Xiyun; Xingyang Guijing points to Shaoshi, Shoushan Shengnian to a personal transmission there, Baizhang Zhiying to an image held in the palm, and Qingshan Hao to a charge received at Vulture Peak and enacted at Wenshui. Konggu Daocheng speaks of fanning this style until plants come alive, Juelang Dasheng asks supporters to sustain it together, and Guxue Zhe says it will greatly flourish. Chan bends ordinary school custom into an inheritance whose validity is made public in answers and conduct.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 2,159 exact hits in 337 files and 331 works. One referent covers inheritance, activation, support, and flourishing; response differences are lineage claims, not separate senses.
